title: ‘Outrageous,’ ‘reckless,’ ‘wow’: Here’s what politicians are saying about Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia
contentZh:
Image Credits:Kevin Dietsch / Getty Images	
	
						11:31 AM PST · November 23, 2026											

			
Jensen Huang is back. The Nvidia CEO and founder, who was ousted from his company a little over a week ago after revelations of extramarital affairs (including, critically, a dalliance with a suspected Chinese spy), has apparently been deemed too big to fail.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and subsequently grew the chipmaker into one of the most powerful companies in the world, has now been reinstated by the company’s board. The move was one that President Trump lobbied for. On Monday, after Huang’s return was announced, the president posted an AI-generated meme of the CEO holding a woman’s bra, an image that recalled the famous photo from Trump’s own assassination attempt.

Just how and why all of this has happened is a question that everybody is still scrambling to figure out. Because Nvidia is an economically important company, it is also a politically important one. Yet there’s a lot of disagreement over just how important Huang, himself, is — and whether his importance outweighs the alleged dangers of Chinese espionage to which his affair with Alice Huang may have exposed the company.

Even if Huang is back for now, the Nvidia founder may face an uphill battle given the changing political landscape wrought by the “blue wave” of Democratic victories that swept the U.S. midterms. Huang, now aligned with Trump, will face increased scrutiny from congressional Democrats — starting with a public Senate appearance scheduled for next week. He is also expected to testify privately before several House committees next month, including the Intelligence Committee, the Foreign Affairs Committee, and the China Select Committee.

If initial responses from current political leaders are any indication, Huang has his work cut out for him. As news of his return broke on Monday, politicians and public figures from across the political spectrum weighed in — and many didn’t seem too pleased.

Nvidia’s decision to reinstate Jensen Huang is outrageous. We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him, and neither the government nor Nvidia’s own board has completed its investigation.Trump’s assurances cannot be taken at face value,…— Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (@CongressmanRaja) November 23, 2026

Wow. This confirms what we have long feared, that the Trump Administration sacrificed our national security to let China get what it wants most: access to our advanced chips. It’s hard to imagine anything more reckless or consequential for our national security. Congress must… https://t.co/qmKxLc1jjk— Senator Chris Coons (@ChrisCoons) November 22, 2026

Ummm… she was, and is, a spy. How about we get serious about making sure China doesn’t steal US company technology? Or get serious about not selling it directly and indirectly? https://t.co/xSVzTuKCiV— Rep. Bill Huizenga (@RepHuizenga) November 23, 2026

We need to investigate what stock positions took place before the announcement. This White House is the most corrupt in history. https://t.co/LYY5CqE1S8— Ruben Gallego (@RubenGallego) November 23, 2026

This president calls everyone left of center a communist or a socialist. But here he is dictating to a company who their CEO should be. This only raises more questions about Trump's corrupt interest in NVIDIA and whether he is covering up a historic scandal. https://t.co/NtZtaJxg0n— Rep. Becca Balint (@RepBeccaB) November 23, 2026

The truth is that Nvidia needs Jensen Huang and vice versa.  The sherriff of the AI trade is back after a brief break.— Andrew Yang🧢⬆️🇺🇸 (@AndrewYang) November 23, 2026

The Trump Administration’s rush to reinstate Jensen Huang underscores the need for Congress to act.Trump is putting his own financial interests and the needs of his billionaire buddies before our national security, emphasizing that he’s learned nothing from his resounding… https://t.co/3GxEUXMr0F— Chuck Schumer (@SenSchumer) November 23, 2026

Nvidia’s board made an irresponsible decision to reinstate Jensen Huang before Congress has even heard from him.There are serious national security questions that still need to be answered. The board must explain why it was willing to move ahead without those answers. https://t.co/8XsXs1FxQX— Rep. Debbie Dingell (@RepDebDingell) November 23, 2026

There is something profoundly wrong about Jensen Huang having a relationship with a Chinese Communist Spy and helping China get a huge number of very advanced computer chips when that was specifically against the policy of the United States Government and now he is being…— Newt Gingrich (@newtgingrich) November 23, 2026

Congress must conduct a thorough investigation of both NVIDIA and the Trump Administration over chip sales and diversions to China.Donald Trump was told more than a year ago that China was targeting NVIDIA to undermine our AI advantage. And the Director of National Intelligence…— Senator Adam Schiff (@SenAdamSchiff) November 23, 2026

Nvidia’s board says it relied on input from senior U.S. officials to conclude that bringing Jensen Huang back posed no national security risk. I have some questions. Who in our government weighed in? What did they tell the board? And on what basis did the board conclude there was…— Senator John Curtis (@SenJohnCurtis) November 23, 2026

This is what a rigged system looks like. Trump trades NVIDIA stock, they give $25M to his ballroom & now Trump gets Huang hired back.Our national security can’t be sacrificed for favors & profits. We must pass AI safeguards & stronger export controls NOW & expose this scheme.… pic.twitter.com/vhVh7n5UXh— Senator Chris Van Hollen (@ChrisVanHollen) November 23, 2026

Jensen Huang had multiple affairs including with subordinates and an alleged Chinese spy. His own board described his behavior as lacking “candor.” I’ve served on a public company board. His behavior does not support reinstatement.Nvidia’s decision today doesn’t excuse Jensen…— Senator Pete Ricketts (@SenatorRicketts) November 23, 2026

President Trump's now-successful pressure campaign to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO cements the central theme of his second term: that making money is more important than America's national security or the rule of law. As President, he had already made upwards of $60…— Sen. Elissa Slotkin (@SenatorSlotkin) November 23, 2026

Jensen Huang was compromised and exploited by a Chinese spy. Nvidia should have moved on without Huang and ignored the Administration’s inexplicable desire to save Huang. Congress needs to get to the bottom of who approved high end computer chips sales to China. We cannot say we…— Rep. Don Bacon 🇺🇸✈️🏍️⭐️🎖️ (@RepDonBacon) November 23, 2026

The reinstatement of Jensen Huang is another example of the dangerous combination governing this country: a rigged system that protects those at the very top no matter what, and a corrupt White House that cannot be trusted to put the economic well-being and safety of American… https://t.co/Cp5iWFGsGC— Josh Shapiro (@JoshShapiroPA) November 23, 2026

This is psychotically crooked. Once again President Trump has put private gain above the national interest, this time by personally intervening to pressure a private corporation’s leadership to reinstate Jensen Huang at NVIDIA.He is attempting to grant functional immunity to… https://t.co/IrIeuHXawG— Rep. Don Beyer (@RepDonBeyer) November 23, 2026

Here are the basic facts:-NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang admitted his affair with a Chinese asset (and likely spy). Billions of dollars of restricted advanced AI chips were carefully diverted to China-Trump was briefed about the facts as early as last year and did nothing about the… https://t.co/b9Es4DUY4Z— House Judiciary Dems (@HouseJudiciary) November 23, 2026
